units.summary: ParseQuantity now calls CacheString on the slow int64 path and the big-decimal path, so every parsed Quantity has its canonical string cached. This replaces the lazy caching that String() used to do.
units.headline: ParseQuantity now eagerly caches canonical string
units.reason: Changes the state of every parsed Quantity (the unexported s field) and adds work to a hot parse path.
focus: Every successful return path in ParseQuantity sets s
Extra parse cost versus the lazy approach
Callers comparing Quantities with reflect.DeepEqual

units.summary: String no longer writes the computed string back to the receiver. It returns the cached value if present and otherwise recomputes it on each call. This removes a data race on concurrent reads, but quantities built without ParseQuantity pay the full cost on every call.
units.headline: String() no longer mutates receiver; recomputes when uncached
units.reason: Changes caching and mutation semantics of a widely used method, with concurrency and performance consequences.
focus: Quantities from NewQuantity/MustParse-less paths now recompute on each String/Marshal call
Encoders that call String twice (Size then Marshal)
Whether any code relied on String populating q.s

units.summary: Adds a public CacheString method that computes the canonical string and always stores it in q.s. It returns "<nil>" for a nil receiver. It is intended for callers that own the instance.
units.headline: Add public Quantity.CacheString that stores canonical string
units.reason: New public API that mutates the receiver, and the doc contract about when it is safe to call matters.
focus: Unconditional write is deliberate and racy if called on shared instances
Stale cache if called before a later mutation (math ops reset s)

units.summary: The test now expects ParseQuantity to set the cached string. It no longer expects String() to populate it. This changes assertions to match the new behavior.
units.headline: Test expects ParseQuantity, not String, to populate cache
units.reason: Test expectations were changed to match new behavior, which the rules treat as needing human review.
focus: The new assertion still verifies String() equals the canonical form
Nothing now checks that String() leaves q.s empty for uncached quantities

units.summary: A new test covers CacheString: it populates q.s, is idempotent, and returns "<nil>" for a nil receiver.
units.headline: New test for CacheString behavior
units.reason: Test-only addition with no production effect.

units.summary: The benchmark now runs sub-benchmarks per quantity using b.Loop, and the precalculated variant is removed.
units.headline: Benchmark restructured into per-quantity sub-benchmarks
units.reason: Benchmark-only restructuring, with no production impact.

units.summary: The benchmark is converted to per-quantity sub-benchmarks with b.Loop.
units.headline: BinarySI string benchmark uses sub-benchmarks
units.reason: Benchmark-only change.

units.summary: The benchmark now parses every test-case input as its own sub-benchmark.
units.headline: ParseQuantity benchmark iterates over test-case inputs
